subject: Response elongation and error-rate spike — Stitchline production impact
messages:
From: Seth Miller <seth.miller@stitchline.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@stitchline.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Stitchline production: sudden response elongation and increased 5xx rate

Hi Logan —

We started seeing a regressive behavior around 08:45 PT this morning: a ~0.8% 5xx rate and a long tail of responses that used to be 150–300ms now spiking into the multiple-second range for ~2–3% of requests. Checkout flows are timing out for some customers.

Attached is a small sampling of request IDs and traces (stitchline_latency_log_20270405.zip). The traces show queues waiting before model invocation and then long token-generation stretches. Can you confirm whether this is a model-side regression, a routing/backpressure problem, or something on our end? This is impacting our busiest region right now — we need a 2–4 hour mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Seth Miller
Head of Platform — Stitchline
seth.miller@stitchline.com

---
Note: I've CC'd Ana who can share more telemetry if needed.

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Seth Miller <seth.miller@stitchline.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@stitchline.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Stitchline production: sudden response elongation and increased 5xx rate

Seth —

Thanks for the heads up and the traces, Ana. We've kicked off an urgent triage. Monica (SRE) is already looking at the GPU pool metrics and request queue depths. Initial ask: can you confirm whether these requests used the same model variant and what the typical prompt length distribution looked like for the 08:30–09:00 PT window?

Immediate mitigations we're considering:
- temporary routing to a lower-capacity-compatible variant (fewer KV-cache pressure points)
- increase per-instance concurrency cap for the dedicated pool serving your workspace (short-term)
- enable additional prefix/KV cache warming for the most common prefixes you sent this morning

I propose a 30-min call with stitchline engineering + our on-call SRE + me to decide the short-term switch. Monica, can you pull the per-node queue metrics and estimate how many requests were queued vs processed?

Logan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Attachment: request-ids-sample.txt (referenced in stitched zip)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Seth Miller <seth.miller@stitchline.com>, Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@stitchline.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Stitchline production: sudden response elongation and increased 5xx rate

On Tue, Apr 5, 2027 at 09:36 Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica (SRE) is already looking at the GPU pool metrics and request queue depths.

Summary of what I'm seeing (quick, from live dashboards):
- For the Stitchline dedicated pool: 60% of requests were held in per-shard request queues for >1500ms during the 08:40–08:55PT window.
- Per-instance CPU/GPUs are not saturated overall; the KV-cache miss rate jumped ~12% which correlates with the longer generation window per-request.
- There is a spike in short lived bursts from a small subset of client IDs that appear to be sending longer prompts than usual (avg prompt tokens from those IDs up ~3x).
- Concurrency cap on the pool was at the configured safe-default of 64 per instance. During the burst we saw queueing because a small number of requests pinned up long token-generation times and occupied concurrency slots.

Preliminary hypothesis: a combination of sudden prompt-length skew and KV-cache churn leading to per-instance tokens churn (cold-KV misses), plus conservative per-instance concurrency caps resulted in queueing ripple and some 5xx timeouts when queued requests exceeded internal timeouts.

Immediate actions taken (09:50 PT):
- Raised instance concurrency cap from 64 -> 96 for the affected pool (manual, temporary).
- Applied aggressive prefix cache warming for top 20 prefixes from the attached sample_trace_profile.txt.
- Enabled fallback routing to a capacity-optimized variant for new sessions from the affected client IDs.

Next steps:
- Dieg0 (Diego), can you validate whether the increased concurrency introduced any scheduling latencies on the nodes?
- We recommend a short-term quota throttle on the misbehaving client IDs to prevent repeated bursts while we investigate a long-term mitigation.

I'll update after we observe the change for 30 minutes.

Monica
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Seth Miller <seth.miller@stitchline.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Stitchline production: sudden response elongation and increased 5xx rate

Monica —

Validation from perf traces (10:20 PT snapshot):
- The raised concurrency cap did not introduce extra scheduling latency on GPU kernels; instance-level utilization remains within headroom (avg GPU util ~72%).
- KV cache warming reduced cold-miss-related generation pauses; average token-gen tail dropped by ~35% for warmed prefixes.
- Fallback routing diverted ~22% of incoming sessions to the capacity-optimized variant with slightly higher per-token cost but >90% of those sessions returned to <500ms median latency.
- We observed two 5xxs caused by internal request-timeout thresholds while a request was queued for >8s (these are the ones stitchline flagged). We've raised our internal request-timeout on the affected route from 10s -> 14s temporarily to avoid hard failures while we finish root cause analysis.

Impact after mitigations (10:25 PT): 5xx rate down from ~0.8% -> 0.12%. Tail-long requests (>=2s) from 2.9% -> 0.4%.

Recommendation:
1) Keep the raised concurrency cap and timeout temporarily for 48 hours while we run a replay / workload analysis.
2) Schedule a post-mortem with Stitchline: identify the client-side changes that produced the prompt-length skew and discuss usage-rate throttles or client-side batching.
3) Product to evaluate an automatic adaptive concurrency policy for dedicated pools: tighten when cold-cache churn detected, relax when warmed.

Evelyn — tagging for exec visibility; this triggered a short SLA-impact conversation with the customer.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Runtime Performance — Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Seth Miller <seth.miller@stitchline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T17:45:00Z
Subject: Stitchline mitigation recap and next steps

Seth / Ana —

Quick recap and commitments after today's mitigation work:
- Symptoms: transient spike in long-tail response times and a modest 5xx rate caused by queueing from long prompt bursts + KV-cache cold-miss churn on the dedicated pool.
- Immediate mitigation: concurrency cap bump, prefix cache warming, and fallback routing to capacity-optimized variant. These reduced the 5xxs and long-tail within an hour.
- Short-term commitments (48 hours): we will keep the concurrency cap at 96 for the affected pool, maintain the extended request-timeout for the affected route, and continue cache-warmers for the top prefixes.
- Medium-term actions (2 weeks): joint post-mortem, client-side prompt-distribution sanity checks, and evaluation of an adaptive concurrency controller that uses live KV-cache churn signals.

Action items:
- Redwood (Logan/Monica/Diego): deliver a post-mortem write-up and a recommended adaptive concurrency design by 2027-04-12.
- Stitchline (Seth/Ana): share the client churn events and any deploys that coincided with 08:30–09:00 PT window.

We'll schedule the post-mortem for next week; I'll send a calendar invite. If you want executive-level notes for your leadership, Evelyn is happy to join a 15-minute readout.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — please ping if anything degrades.

Best,
Logan Wright
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: stitchline_latency_log_20270405.zip, sample_trace_profile.txt

On behalf of the team: Monica Patel (SRE), Diego Fernandez (Runtime Performance), Evelyn Hart (Head of Customer Escalations)
